newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids hold despite crude slide, weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids hold despite crude slide, weather.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly held steady Thursday in thin pre-holiday trade, with tight supply and some leftover utility interest supporting values despite sinking crude and milder weather forecasts.

"There isn't a lot of low sulphur supply, and demand has been pretty steady. We've been seeing a lot of contract suppliers looking for barrels for utilities," said one cash trader, noting Florida demand has been good and Mexico was still looking for barrels.
New York Harbor one percent cargoes were still talked at $17 a barrel, with prompt barges pegged closer to $17.25-50.
NYH August one percent paper fell 20-30 cents to the $16.60-90 area with weaker crude.
NYH 0.3 high pour firmed slightly to the $18.30-55 area. Traders said 50,000 barrels of prompt 0.33 percent (high viscosity) sold at $18.80.
New York high sulphurs were steady, with 2.2 percent still quoted at $15.00-25. Traders said 200,000 barrels of prompt 2.4 percent sold at $15.40 (delivered Wilmington, N.C.).
Temperatures next week in the Midwest and Northeast are expected to stay below-normal, with normal weather forecast for the Gulf Coast and Florida.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent held at $15.50, while three percent was flat at about $13.75.
USG high sulphur was still buoyed by reports of some Mexican buying.

New York city gate weekend gas prices slipped a few cents Thursday to the mid-$2.30s/mmBtu, or $14.81 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, was two cents lower at about $2.11/mmBtu, or $13.29 a barrel.
NYMEX will be closed Friday for the Independence Day holiday.
